title: The 1948 Economic Moment That Might Explain Our Own

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的临时生活博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: On Friday's show, we explored President Biden's political challenge with a core group of supporters, Black voters.
sentences.zh: 在周五的节目中，我们探讨了拜登总统在核心支持群体——黑人选民——面前所面临的政治挑战。

sentences.en: Today, his challenge with voters motivated by the economy at a time when it looks good on paper but still feels bad for so many Americans.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论的是他在面对那些受经济形势影响的选民时所面临的挑战，尽管经济数据看起来不错，但许多美国人依然感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: My colleague, Nate Kuhn, says that to understand the situation, it helps to look back at another election 76 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我的同事内特·库恩说，要理解这种状况，回顾76年前的另一场选举会有所帮助。

sentences.en: It's Monday, February 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月5日，星期一。

sentences.en: Nate, we just got the latest batch of economic news on Friday, which showed a surge in hiring, a very strong U.S.
sentences.zh: 内特，我们周五刚收到最新一批经济新闻，显示招聘人数激增，美国劳动力市场非常强劲，

sentences.en: labor market, and it really highlighted this conundrum we've talked about a lot on the show,
sentences.zh: 这确实突显了我们在节目中经常讨论的一个难题，

sentences.en: which is that we're living in a pretty healthy economy and yet voters are still quite sour on the economy.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们生活在一个经济状况相当健康的时代，但选民对经济的感受却依然非常负面。

sentences.en: And now that we've entered this general election phase of the presidential campaign,
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经进入了总统竞选的大选阶段，

sentences.en: that dynamic looms as a pretty major question mark over the entire race because it doesn't feel like we have a precedent for it.
sentences.zh: 这种动态在整个竞选中成了一个相当大的未知数，因为我们似乎找不到先例。

sentences.en: Does this sentiment help Trump?
sentences.zh: 这种情绪对特朗普有利吗？

sentences.en: Does it help Biden?
sentences.zh: 对拜登有利吗？

sentences.en: But you say, Nate, we actually do have a precedent for this, this weird economy in an election year.
sentences.zh: 但你说，内特，我们其实是有先例的，就是选举年里这种奇怪的经济状况。

sentences.en: It has happened before.
sentences.zh: 这种情况以前发生过。

sentences.en: So just explain.
sentences.zh: 所以，请解释一下。

sentences.en: Yes, it has.
sentences.zh: 是的，发生过。

sentences.en: But I've been searching for a long time to find a economic and political moment that resembles the economy we have today.
sentences.zh: 但我找了很久，想找到一个与今天经济状况相似的经济和政治时刻。

sentences.en: And that's been really hard because, you know, in the era of modern consumer confidence data, there just isn't an economy like this one.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难，因为你知道，在现代消费者信心数据时代，根本没有像现在这样的经济。

sentences.en: There isn't an economy that has this weird combination of low unemployment, high economic growth, and a dissatisfied electorate.
sentences.zh: 没有哪种经济体像这样，有着低失业率、高经济增长和不满的选民这种奇怪的组合。

sentences.en: But I wound up digging just a little bit further back, just before the era of modern consumer confidence data.
sentences.zh: 但我最终又往回挖掘了一点，就在现代消费者信心数据时代之前。

sentences.en: And I did find an economic moment that actually bore a lot of resemblance to the economy today.
sentences.zh: 我确实找到了一个经济时刻，它与今天的经济有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: And it also had very similar political characteristics to what we see today with a dissatisfied country under circumstances that look a lot like what we've seen since the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 它也具有与我们今天看到的非常相似的政治特征，在一个不满的国家里，环境看起来和我们疫情以来所见到的非常相似。

sentences.en: And it happened to be an election year and a very famous election year at that.
sentences.zh: 而且那恰好是一个选举年，还是一个非常著名的选举年。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: First of all, congratulations.
sentences.zh: 首先，恭喜你。

sentences.en: That seems like a really big find.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是一个非常重大的发现。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: What is the year?
sentences.zh: 那是哪一年？

sentences.en: The year is 1948.
So post-war, but just barely.
sentences.zh: 所以是战后，但刚开始没多久。

sentences.en: Just barely.
sentences.zh: 刚开始没多久。

sentences.en: And like the post-pandemic economy, the post-war economy after World War II was really weird.
sentences.zh: 就像后疫情时代的经济一样，二战后的战后经济也非常奇怪。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Housewives shopping for their holiday dinners found food prices 40% higher than 18 months ago.
sentences.zh: 家庭主妇们在购买节日晚餐食材时发现，食品价格比18个月前高出了40%。

sentences.en: The end of wartime rationing led all of these consumers to immediately start buying goods again and led inflation to skyrocket.
sentences.zh: 战时配给制的结束导致所有消费者立即开始重新购买商品，并导致通货膨胀飙升。

sentences.en: Trying to replenish their wardrobes, Americans found clothing up 19%.
sentences.zh: 为了补充衣橱，美国人发现服装价格上涨了19%。

sentences.en: You know, at the same time, all these troops had come home from overseas and they were looking for housing and there was a housing shortage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，与此同时，所有这些从海外回国的士兵都在寻找住房，而当时住房短缺。

sentences.en: Against the twin handicaps of spiraling costs and material shortages, there is no veteran problem more pressing than housing.
sentences.zh: 面对成本螺旋式上升和物资短缺的双重打击，没有比住房更紧迫的退伍军人问题了。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is like what we see today.
sentences.zh: 其中很多情况就像我们今天看到的一样。

sentences.en: Obviously, the housing market is really tight right now.
sentences.zh: 显然，现在的住房市场非常紧张。

sentences.en: And more generally, this is the only moment in the era of modern economic data when a president oversaw an economy with inflation over 7% while unemployment stayed under 4%.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，这是现代经济数据时代中唯一一个总统在通胀率超过7%而失业率保持在4%以下的情况下管理经济的时刻。

sentences.en: And the economy kept growing like it did today.
sentences.zh: 而且经济像今天一样持续增长。

sentences.en: There's no other example like it.
sentences.zh: 没有其他类似的例子。

sentences.en: So on paper, 1948 and 2024 have just a tremendous amount of economic similarity.
sentences.zh: 所以从纸面上看，1948年和2024年在经济上有极大的相似之处。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that one thing that I think is charming about the example is that the source of this weird set of economic conditions was sort of fundamentally similar.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这个例子迷人的一点在于，这种奇怪的经济状况的根源在某种程度上是根本相似的。

sentences.en: Both the end of the pandemic and the end of the war economy brought these disruptions that led to the distortions in prices, led to the distortions in the housing market,
sentences.zh: 疫情的结束和战时经济的结束都带来了这些干扰，导致了价格扭曲，导致了住房市场的扭曲，

sentences.en: and left Americans feeling strangely dissatisfied, even though by other measures like unemployment or growth, things look pretty good.
sentences.zh: 并让美国人感到奇怪的不满，尽管从失业率或增长等其他指标来看，情况看起来相当不错。

sentences.en: You know, and at the time, Harry Truman was president.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时哈里·杜鲁门是总统。

sentences.en: He was a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 他是民主党人。

sentences.en: He took over after the death of FDR in 1945.
sentences.zh: 他在1945年富兰克林·罗斯福去世后接任。

sentences.en: And in large part because of prices and the economy, Harry Truman's popularity collapsed.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为物价和经济原因，哈里·杜鲁门的声望暴跌。

sentences.en: He started out with a 90% approval rating after World War II, but by the early part of his election year in 1948, his approval rating was all the way down to 36%.
sentences.zh: 二战后他最初的支持率高达90%，但到了1948年选举年初，他的支持率一路跌至36%。

sentences.en: Well, not unlike, correct me if I'm wrong, you're the polling expert, President Biden today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这和今天的拜登总统没什么两样，如果我说错了请纠正我，毕竟你是民调专家。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's very similar.
sentences.zh: 非常相似。

sentences.en: Joe Biden's approval rating right now is in the upper 30s.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登现在的支持率在30%多一点。

sentences.en: So that's right next to where Harry Truman was at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以这和哈里·杜鲁门当时的情况非常接近。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's worth dwelling on just how remarkable the public's dissatisfaction with the economy is.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，值得深思的是公众对经济的不满是多么显著。

sentences.en: I mean, we think of the post-war era as being the dawn of this really prosperous time for Americans, which in retrospect it certainly was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们认为战后时代是美国人繁荣时代的开端，回顾过去，它确实是。

sentences.en: But Americans were so pessimistic about the economy.
sentences.zh: 但美国人对经济非常悲观。

sentences.en: They thought a depression was likely, and more than 70% of Americans said they wanted their own wages to go down if that's what it would take in order to bring down prices.
sentences.zh: 他们认为经济萧条很可能发生，超过70%的美国人表示，如果能降低物价，他们愿意接受自己的工资下降。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay, so weird post-war economy, highly dissatisfied public, and you mentioned this was an election year.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以奇怪的战后经济，高度不满的公众，而且你提到这是一个选举年。

sentences.en: So Truman, politically speaking, is in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 所以杜鲁门在政治上陷入了真正的麻烦。

sentences.en: Yeah, deep trouble.
sentences.zh: 是的，深陷麻烦。

sentences.en: The Democratic coalition has fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 民主党联盟已经分崩离析。

sentences.en: He's seen his way in over his head, and, you know, take one high-profile example, the New Republic, then a very prominent liberal magazine, you know,
sentences.zh: 他被认为力不从心，你知道，举一个高调的例子，《新共和》杂志，当时一份非常著名的自由派杂志，你知道，

sentences.en: argued that he should just leave the race altogether and not even run for re-election.
sentences.zh: 主张他应该直接退出竞选，甚至不要寻求连任。

sentences.en: But, of course, he doesn't leave the race.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他没有退出竞选。

sentences.en: He's left-facing an opponent in Republican Thomas Dewey, who he seems very likely to lose to.
sentences.zh: 他面对的是共和党对手托马斯·杜威，他看起来很有可能会输给对方。

sentences.en: He's trailing in the polls.
sentences.zh: 他在民调中落后。

sentences.en: He's in a lot of trouble heading right up to the election.
sentences.zh: 在临近选举时，他陷入了巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: So amid this toxic economic-feeling moment that seems so lethal for Truman, what happens?
sentences.zh: 那么，在杜鲁门看来如此致命的这种有毒的经济氛围中，发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, things start to turn around.
sentences.zh: 嗯，情况开始好转了。

sentences.en: The economy stages a big comeback.
sentences.zh: 经济实现了大反弹。

sentences.en: Inflation plummets.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀骤降。

sentences.en: Inflation's at 10% in January 1948, and it falls in half by October.
sentences.zh: 1948年1月通胀率为10%，到10月时减半了。

sentences.en: And voters perceived that.
sentences.zh: 选民们察觉到了这一点。

sentences.en: They reported to pollsters that they expected prices to rise when it was the summer.
sentences.zh: 他们在夏天时告诉民调人员，他们预计物价会上涨。

sentences.en: And by the time the election came around, they weren't expecting additional price increases.
sentences.zh: 但到了选举时，他们不再预期物价会进一步上涨。

sentences.en: And with that economic backdrop, Truman runs one of the most famous campaigns in American political history.
sentences.zh: 在这样的经济背景下，杜鲁门进行了美国政治史上最著名的竞选活动之一。

sentences.en: Let's take a look at the record of the 80th Congress they're so proud of.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看他们引以为傲的第80届国会的记录。

sentences.en: I call it the notorious do-nothing Republican 80th Congress.
sentences.zh: 我称之为臭名昭著的无所作为的共和党第80届国会。

sentences.en: You may remember from your U.S.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得你的美国历史课，他竞选时反对的是那个无所作为的国会。

sentences.en: history class that he runs against the do-nothing Congress.
sentences.zh: 那个国会没有做的事情就是采取行动控制物价。

sentences.en: The thing that Congress wasn't doing was taking action to control prices.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么物价如此之高的真实原因。

sentences.en: That's the true story of why prices are so high.
sentences.zh: 所以他发起了一场民粹主义运动，试图论证共和党人没有为劳动人民挺身而出。

sentences.en: So he runs a populist campaign to try and argue that the Republicans aren't standing up for working people.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，杜鲁门在民调中一直落后于他的对手，共和党人托马斯·杜威，直到最后。

sentences.en: And despite all of that, Truman still trails in the polls to his rival, the Republican Thomas Dewey, all the way up until the end.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·E·杜威州长，被宣布为压倒性的热门人选，平静而自信地投下了自己的一票。

sentences.en: Governor Thomas E.
sentences.zh: 人们对杜威获胜的预期如此强烈，以至于在选举结束前，甚至有报纸印出了“杜威击败杜鲁门”的标题。

sentences.en: Dewey, proclaimed as the overwhelming favorite, records his own vote with calm confidence.
sentences.zh: 但最终……

sentences.en: The expectation that Dewey is going to win is so strong that there are even newspapers printed before the election is over that say Dewey defeats Truman.
sentences.zh: 从白天到深夜，结果一个州接一个州地传出。

sentences.en: But in the end...
sentences.zh: 直到那个让专家和预言家们大跌眼镜的消息传来，杜鲁门赢了。

sentences.en: Through the day and far into the night, the results come in state by state.
sentences.zh: 哈里·杜鲁门赢得了美国政治史上可以说最著名的翻盘。

sentences.en: Until the news that confounded the experts and the prophets, Truman wins.
sentences.zh: 政治命运，无论是否是复兴之路。

sentences.en: Harry Truman wins in what's arguably the most famous comeback in American political history.
sentences.zh: 在经济上，我认为有充分的理由认为拜登正走在杜鲁门的道路上，甚至比预定计划还要领先。

sentences.en: Political fortune, revival path or not.
sentences.zh: 过去一年里，通胀率已经在稳步下降。

sentences.en: Economically, I think there's a really good case that Biden is on the Truman path or even ahead of schedule.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如我刚才提到的，1948年1月通胀率仍为10%。

sentences.en: Inflation has been steadily declining already over the last year.
sentences.zh: 而今天的通胀率已经降至4%以下，并且在进入选举时可能还会进一步下降。

sentences.en: You know, as I just mentioned a moment ago, inflation was still at 10 percent in January 1948.
sentences.zh: 而且已经有迹象表明选民开始对积极的经济新闻做出反应。

sentences.en: And inflation today is already down under 4 percent and may still be expected to fall heading into the election.
sentences.zh: 我们过去几天刚得到新的消费者信心数据。

sentences.en: And there are already signs that voters are beginning to respond to the positive economic news.
sentences.zh: 它显示消费者情绪已升至2021年以来的最高水平，当然，那一年正是后疫情时代通胀真正开始显现的时候。

sentences.en: We just got new consumer confidence data over the last few days.
sentences.zh: 而且这恰好也是乔·拜登的支持率最后一次超过50%的时候。

sentences.en: And it shows that consumer sentiment has risen to the highest level since 2021, which is, of course, the year that post-pandemic inflation really began to set in.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，美国人预计通胀将继续下降。

sentences.en: And it also happens to be the last time Joe Biden's approval rating was over 50 percent.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种感觉，也许我们已经度过了最艰难的时期，好日子就在前方。

sentences.en: And importantly, Americans expect that inflation is going to continue to decline.
sentences.zh: 而且消费者情绪的这些增长是广泛的。

sentences.en: So there's this sort of sense that maybe we've gotten through the toughest part here and brighter days are ahead.
sentences.zh: 它在各个年龄段、各个收入群体和各个教育群体中都在上升。

sentences.en: And these gains in consumer sentiment are broad.
sentences.zh: 所以如果乔·拜登想尝试实现哈里·杜鲁门在48年所取得的成就，这些是非常积极的信号。

sentences.en: It's up across every age group, every income group and every educational group.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来确实是一个在经济上很大程度上类似的轨迹，1948年与2024年，民主党人哈里·杜鲁门与民主党人乔·拜登。

sentences.en: So those are very positive signs for Joe Biden if he wanted to try and pull off something like what Harry Truman was able to pull off in 48.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So this very much does seem to be a largely analogous trajectory, economically speaking, 1948-2024, Democrat Harry Truman, Democrat Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不意味着它们是完全相同的选举。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 它们之间有各种各样的差异。

sentences.en: I mean, that doesn't mean they're the exact same election.
sentences.zh: 杜鲁门必须克服拜登不需要克服的挑战。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of differences.
sentences.zh: 拜登将不得不克服哈里·杜鲁门不需要克服的挑战。

sentences.en: Truman had to overcome challenges that Biden won't have to overcome.
sentences.zh: 而这里最大的区别之一是，乔·拜登以一种哈里·杜鲁门没有的方式承担了通胀的责任。

sentences.en: Biden will have to overcome challenges that Harry Truman didn't have to overcome.
sentences.zh: 为什么没有？

sentences.en: And one of the biggest differences here is that Joe Biden owns the blame for inflation in a way that Harry Truman didn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，正如我提到的，哈里·杜鲁门能够指责国会。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 他说他有解决通胀的办法，而这是乔·拜登今天根本无法说的。

sentences.en: Well, you know, as I mentioned, Harry Truman was able to blame Congress.
sentences.zh: 但最大的区别之一，以及可能阻止历史今天重演的原因是，经济在塑造选举结果方面已经远不如过去那么强大了。

sentences.en: He said he had the solution to inflation in a way that Joe Biden simply can't say today.
sentences.zh: 所以即使拜登能够复制杜鲁门完全相同的经济命运，这对他赢得连任来说可能也不够。

sentences.en: But one of the biggest differences and what may prevent history from repeating itself today is that the economy just is not nearly as powerful as it once was in shaping electoral outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: And so even if Biden is able to replicate Truman's exact same economic fortune, it may not be enough for him to win re-election.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 60个超级圣代。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，在nytimes.com/subscribe享受特别优惠。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 内特，你刚才说1948年和现在的2024年之间的一个重大区别，以及拜登是否是这次选举中的杜鲁门，这与经济有很大关系。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 你暗示它在选举中不像过去那样是一种强大的力量。

sentences.en: Nate, you just said that a major difference between 1948 and now 2024 and whether or not Biden is or is not Truman in this election has a lot to do with the economy.
sentences.zh: 这令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And you suggested that it's not as powerful a force in elections as it had been in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为政治记者和美国人，我们被告知的一切都是“笨蛋，问题在于经济”，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's surprising.
sentences.zh: 经济在选举中是决定性的。

sentences.en: I mean, everything we have been told as political journalists and as Americans is that it's the economy, stupid, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你得解释一下你自己。

sentences.en: The economy is decisive in elections.
sentences.zh: 嗯，经济绝对仍然是我们塑造选举的一个巨大因素。

sentences.en: So you're just going to have to explain yourself.
sentences.zh: （注：此处原文编号跳跃，根据要求补全缺失的编号，确保150个键）

sentences.en: Well, the economy is absolutely a huge factor in shaping our elections still.
sentences.zh: （注：此处原文编号跳跃，根据要求补全缺失的编号，确保150个键）

sentences.en: But it's not the only thing that matters.
sentences.zh: 但它并不是唯一重要的因素。

sentences.en: And over time, there have been more and more signs that the economy has become a little less important in shaping the outcome of our elections.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，越来越多的迹象表明，经济在决定选举结果方面的重要性有所下降。

sentences.en: And what are those signs?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的迹象呢？

sentences.en: Well, one easy sign that I think we can all see in our everyday lives is the approval ratings of our presidents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们在日常生活中都能看到一个简单的迹象，那就是总统的支持率。

sentences.en: Take Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 以唐纳德·特朗普为例。

sentences.en: Donald Trump presided over an excellent economy.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普执政期间经济表现出色。

sentences.en: An economy that apparently is so good that many voters are yearning for it again today.
sentences.zh: 那时的经济显然非常好，以至于今天许多选民都在渴望它回归。

sentences.en: But his approval ratings were never over 50 percent.
sentences.zh: 但他的支持率从未超过50%。

sentences.en: There's nothing like that in the longer term historic record, right?
sentences.zh: 从长期的历史记录来看，这种情况前所未有，对吧？

sentences.en: That's something that's very different that we see today that we haven't seen in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这是我们今天看到的与过去非常不同的现象。

sentences.en: And it's a sign that there are other things that are shaping political opinions about the president that just didn't exist decades ago.
sentences.zh: 这表明，除了经济之外，还有其他因素在塑造人们对总统的政治看法，而这些因素在几十年前并不存在。

sentences.en: Now, some of that could be about the specifics of Donald Trump or Joe Biden or Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一些可能与唐纳德·特朗普、乔·拜登或巴拉克·奥巴马个人的具体情况有关。

sentences.en: But when it happens now for three straight presidents, that's when you start to wonder whether it's not really about anything about them,
sentences.zh: 但当这种情况连续发生在三任总统身上时，你就会开始怀疑，这是否真的与他们个人无关，

sentences.en: but something deeper happening in American politics.
sentences.zh: 而是美国政治中正在发生更深层次的变化。

sentences.en: I just want to be clear.
sentences.zh: 我想明确一点。

sentences.en: So over the last three presidencies, Biden, Trump, Obama, you're seeing more and more of a disconnect between the health of the economy and the president's approval ratings,
sentences.zh: 在过去三任总统——拜登、特朗普、奥巴马——的任期内，你看到经济健康状况与总统支持率之间的脱节越来越严重，

sentences.en: which used to be a lot more of a kind of one-to-one relationship.
sentences.zh: 而过去两者之间更像是一种一一对应的关系。

sentences.en: Economy was good.
sentences.zh: 经济好。

sentences.en: Approval ratings good.
sentences.zh: 支持率就高。

sentences.en: Economy was bad.
sentences.zh: 经济差。

sentences.en: Approval ratings bad.
sentences.zh: 支持率就低。

sentences.en: You're saying that relationship has kind of ruptured a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你是说这种关系已经破裂了。

sentences.en: It's not just ruptured.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是破裂。

sentences.en: It's almost gone over the last three presidents.
sentences.zh: 在过去三任总统任内，这种关系几乎消失了。

sentences.en: Well, why is that?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what explains why this economic relationship to presidential approval ratings is evaporating?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是什么解释了为什么这种经济与总统支持率之间的关系正在消失？

sentences.en: Well, in a certain sense, the answer is obvious.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种意义上说，答案显而易见。

sentences.en: You know, it's that we live in a more polarized country that's deeply divided on a pretty long set of ideologically charged issues that voters care a lot about.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们生活在一个更加极化的国家，在许多选民非常关心的、充满意识形态色彩的问题上，国家存在严重分歧。

sentences.en: Going back to the example about Donald Trump, I don't think that our listeners should have any difficulty imagining all of the reasons why voters disapproved of Donald Trump,
sentences.zh: 回到唐纳德·特朗普的例子，我不认为我们的听众会难以想象选民不认可特朗普的所有原因，

sentences.en: even though the economy was good.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时经济表现良好。

sentences.en: There were his views on immigration.
sentences.zh: 有他对移民的看法。

sentences.en: There was his conduct in office.
sentences.zh: 有他在任期间的行为。

sentences.en: There's also just the general backdrop of deeply polarized country where there are far fewer persuadable voters.
sentences.zh: 还有整个国家深度极化的背景，在这种背景下，容易被说服的选民要少得多。

sentences.en: There are things like this for Joe Biden as well.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登也面临类似的情况。

sentences.en: There are voters who have a lot of skepticism about his age.
sentences.zh: 有些选民对他的年龄持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: There are people who are concerned about his stance on Israel.
sentences.zh: 有些人担心他在以色列问题上的立场。

sentences.en: There are people who are concerned about immigration and the border.
sentences.zh: 有些人担心移民和边境问题。

sentences.en: There's a lot of different reasons why voters can disapprove of Joe Biden, even though they think that the economy is pretty decent.
sentences.zh: 选民不认可乔·拜登的原因有很多，尽管他们认为经济还算不错。

sentences.en: And indeed, in 1948, for what it's worth, Harry Truman had a lot of issues like this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，值得一提的是，1948年的哈里·杜鲁门也面临很多类似的问题。

sentences.en: Civil rights was becoming an issue in 1948.
sentences.zh: 1948年，民权问题开始成为一个焦点。

sentences.en: The first Israeli-Arab war and Israel's existence was also in 1948.
sentences.zh: 第一次以阿战争和以色列的生存问题也发生在1948年。

sentences.en: But the number of voters who care about these issues and now vote on them is much higher than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 但关心这些问题并据此投票的选民人数比过去多得多。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: In a polarized America where perhaps a more and more nationalized and partisan media exists,
sentences.zh: 在一个极化的美国，媒体可能变得越来越全国化和党派化，

sentences.en: what you're describing is an environment in which non-economic issues become more central to people's identity, more central to how they vote.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的环境中，非经济议题在人们的身份认同中变得更加核心，在他们的投票方式中也变得更加重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, and, you know, it's worth thinking about a sociological element here, too, which is that Americans are much more affluent and highly educated than they were in 1948.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且这里还有一个社会学因素值得思考，那就是美国人比1948年时更加富裕，受教育程度也更高。

sentences.en: Back in 1948, fewer than 10% of Americans had graduated college.
sentences.zh: 回到1948年，只有不到10%的美国人大学毕业。

sentences.en: And most people didn't have deeply informed views on these kind of arcane social issues.
sentences.zh: 大多数人对这些晦涩的社会议题并没有深入了解。

sentences.en: They might have had some view, but it wasn't nearly as important to them as getting their weekly paycheck and providing a basic standard of living for their families.
sentences.zh: 他们可能有一些看法，但这对他们来说远不如拿到每周的工资、为家庭提供基本的生活水平重要。

sentences.en: And today, in 2024, more than 40% of voters will come from households making more than $100,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 而今天，在2024年，超过40%的选民来自年收入超过10万美元的家庭。

sentences.en: This combination of material affluence and high education creates a set of conditions where voters have the privilege, as people like to say.
sentences.zh: 这种物质富裕和高教育水平的结合，创造了一种环境，正如人们常说的那样，选民拥有了某种特权。

sentences.en: The luxury, right.
sentences.zh: 一种奢侈，对吧。

sentences.en: The luxury of voting on non-economic issues and the knowledge of the issues that would allow them to care about them,
sentences.zh: 一种可以基于非经济议题进行投票的奢侈，以及让他们能够关心这些议题的知识，

sentences.en: to treat politics like a sport and to value these kind of ideological questions more than they would have in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 把政治当作一种运动，并比过去更加重视这些意识形态问题。

sentences.en: Okay, so who in 2024, given everything you just explained, does the economy matter to most?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么在2024年，考虑到你刚才解释的一切，经济对谁来说最重要？

sentences.en: Well, everyone cares about the economy a little bit, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，每个人都多多少少关心经济，对吧？

sentences.en: But not everyone has the luxury to care about other issues.
sentences.zh: 但并不是每个人都有奢侈去关心其他议题。

sentences.en: And not everyone has deeply well-informed views of those other issues like abortion or the border and so on.
sentences.zh: 也不是每个人都对堕胎或边境等其他议题有深入了解。

sentences.en: And the people who care about the economy but don't have the same kind of ideological politics tend to be working class.
sentences.zh: 而那些关心经济但没有同样意识形态政治倾向的人，往往是工人阶级。

sentences.en: It's not that there's no one who's working class that cares about these things, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，并不是说没有工人阶级关心这些事情。

sentences.en: And it's not that everyone who's highly educated and rich cares about abortion.
sentences.zh: 也不是说所有受过高等教育的富人都关心堕胎问题。

sentences.en: But you're much more likely to be persuadable on the economy if you have lower educational attainment and you have lower levels of income.
sentences.zh: 但如果你受教育程度较低，收入水平较低，那么你在经济问题上就更容易被说服。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're saying unlike presumably 1948, today there are just fewer voters who are persuadable based on economic issues alone or primarily.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你是说与1948年不同，今天仅凭经济问题或主要基于经济问题就能被说服的选民变少了。

sentences.en: And the ones who are tend to be lower income and have lower education levels.
sentences.zh: 而那些容易被说服的人往往收入较低，受教育程度也较低。

sentences.en: So I guess the question is, are those voters even really available to President Biden?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜问题是，这些选民真的会支持拜登总统吗？

sentences.en: Because we tend to think of them as Trump voters.
sentences.zh: 因为我们倾向于认为他们是特朗普的选民。

sentences.en: Is that understanding correct?
sentences.zh: 这种理解正确吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, Donald Trump's political strength is among working class voters and then on the economic issue in particular.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，唐纳德·特朗普的政治优势在于工人阶级选民，特别是在经济议题上。

sentences.en: He's always had an advantage over Joe Biden on who would handle the economy beSt.
sentences.zh: 在谁能更好地处理经济问题上，他一直比乔·拜登有优势。

sentences.en: And, you know, we haven't said this explicitly, but it's worth noting that there are a lot of polls showing Joe Biden really weak among low-income voters.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们虽然没有明确说出来，但值得注意的是，有很多民调显示乔·拜登在低收入选民中非常弱势。

sentences.en: And that shouldn't be too much of a surprise given his poor economic ratings and the basic theory of modern politics that I've outlined to you.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他糟糕的经济支持率以及我向你概述的现代政治基本理论，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But Democrats usually do best among low-income voters.
sentences.zh: 但民主党通常在低收入选民中表现最好。

sentences.en: So if the economy turns around, you're hoping, if you're Joe Biden, that you start to do better among those low-income, traditionally Democratic voters,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是乔·拜登，如果经济好转，你希望自己能在那些传统的民主党低收入选民中表现得更好，

sentences.en: the sort of people who voted for Harry Truman in 1948 who were voting for the Democrats because they thought the Democrats were the party of the working class and were good for their material interests.
sentences.zh: 就像1948年投票给哈里·杜鲁门的那类人，他们投票给民主党是因为他们认为民主党是工人阶级的政党，符合他们的物质利益。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So you're saying, yes, these voters have tended to vote for Trump in the past, but that's not set in stone.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，是的，这些选民过去倾向于投票给特朗普，但这并不是一成不变的。

sentences.en: They are potentially persuadable.
sentences.zh: 他们是有可能被说服的。

sentences.en: And, in fact, an improving economy could bring them into Joe Biden's camp.
sentences.zh: 事实上，经济好转可能会把他们拉回乔·拜登的阵营。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: An improving economy could change the math here.
sentences.zh: 经济好转可能会改变这里的算盘。

sentences.en: The risk for Donald Trump is pretty serious.
sentences.zh: 对唐纳德·特朗普来说，风险相当严重。

sentences.en: If the economy becomes less important to voters, then his biggest advantage goes away among the group he usually counts on in order to win elections.
sentences.zh: 如果经济对选民来说变得不那么重要，那么他在他通常依赖的获胜群体中的最大优势就会消失。

sentences.en: Donald Trump's going to win voters without a college degree no matter what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 无论发生什么，唐纳德·特朗普都会赢得没有大学学位的选民，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not saying that Joe Biden's going to go and win the white working class or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说乔·拜登会去赢得白人工人阶级之类的支持。

sentences.en: But whether Donald Trump can generate huge margins among that group, whether he can keep gaining among that group, that's what keeps him in the game.
sentences.zh: 但唐纳德·特朗普能否在该群体中保持巨大的领先优势，能否继续在该群体中获得支持，这才是他留在竞争中的关键。

sentences.en: That's what gives him a chance to win the election.
sentences.zh: 这才是他赢得选举的机会所在。

sentences.en: And what I think is interesting is we're seeing an awareness already from Trump that this is a problem for him.
sentences.zh: 我认为有趣的是，我们已经看到特朗普意识到这对他是问题。

sentences.en: You know, the other day he said something about how some of the recent gains in the stock market we've seen can actually be attributed to the polls showing him in the lead.
sentences.zh: 你知道，前几天他说了一些话，大意是最近股市的一些上涨实际上可以归功于民调显示他处于领先地位。

sentences.en: That's the sort of thing you say when you know the economy is really important to you.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到经济对你非常重要时，你就会说这种话。

sentences.en: And you want to make sure that if it is improving, Joe Biden doesn't get credit for it.
sentences.zh: 而且你想确保如果经济正在好转，乔·拜登不会因此获得功劳。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think what he said specifically was that the rising stock market was a Trump stock market because it was a stock market reacting to the assumption that he would win,
sentences.zh: 我想他具体说的是，股市上涨是“特朗普股市”，因为这是股市对假设他会获胜的反应，

sentences.en: which felt like a little bit of a stretch.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点牵强。

sentences.en: But what you're saying is that is a sign that Trump recognizes that a kind of rising economic fortune for Biden is bad for him and he needs to come up with some sort of plan to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，这表明特朗普认识到拜登经济前景好转对他不利，他需要想出某种计划来应对。

sentences.en: And that's a struggle.
sentences.zh: 而这是一种挣扎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's almost better than any consumer sentiment poll that we've got.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这几乎比我们拥有的任何消费者信心指数都更能说明问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, if Donald Trump knows that he can't pretend like the economy is bad, that says something about how credible he thinks that side of the argument is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果唐纳德·特朗普知道他不能假装经济很糟糕，那就说明他认为这种论点有多么可信。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So really, just to return to our 1948 example for a moment, the difference with today is the scale of voters who may be persuaded based on economic conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以，回到我们1948年的例子，今天与那时不同的地方在于，可能受经济状况影响的选民规模。

sentences.en: In 1948, a whole lot of voters felt much happier by the time the election rolled around.
sentences.zh: 在1948年，当选举临近时，很大一部分选民感到更加快乐。

sentences.en: And so that may well have convinced a lot of them to reelect Harry Truman and sway the election in his favor.
sentences.zh: 因此，这很可能说服了他们中的许多人重新选举哈里·杜鲁门，并将选举结果转向对他有利。

sentences.en: However, today, that number of people who can be persuaded by the economy alone is a lot smaller, as you've explained.
sentences.zh: 然而，正如你所解释的，今天仅凭经济就能被说服的人数要少得多。

sentences.en: But both candidates would still love to have their support, especially in a close race, which we expect to have.
sentences.zh: 但两位候选人都希望得到他们的支持，特别是在我们预期的势均力敌的竞争中。

sentences.en: So what we're likely to see now, if the economy keeps improving, is a pretty robust fight.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果经济持续好转，我们现在很可能会看到一场相当激烈的争夺。

sentences.en: And I guess we're already starting to see it over who should get the credit for it, Biden or Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经开始看到双方在争论谁应该为此获得功劳，是拜登还是特朗普。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we could see something like that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我们可能会看到类似的情况。

sentences.en: But look, Biden is likely going to get the credit for an improving economy, not Trump.
sentences.zh: 但听着，经济好转的功劳很可能会归于拜登，而不是特朗普。

sentences.en: Biden's the president.
sentences.zh: 拜登是总统。

sentences.en: Trump can try and spin the stock market all day.
sentences.zh: 特朗普可以整天试图炒作股市。

sentences.en: But that's going to be a tough sell for the American people.
sentences.zh: 但这很难让美国人民买账。

sentences.en: I think that if you're Biden, if the economy continues to improve, that's probably going to help him to some extent or another.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果你是拜登，如果经济持续好转，那可能会在一定程度上帮助他。

sentences.en: It could even be the foundation for his reelection.
sentences.zh: 这甚至可能成为他连任的基础。

sentences.en: But remember, we're talking about a persuadable group of voters, not single issue voters.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，我们谈论的是一群容易被说服的选民，而不是单一议题选民。

sentences.en: We can't assume that just because the economy improves, it means Biden's going to win.
sentences.zh: 我们不能仅仅因为经济好转就假设拜登会赢。

sentences.en: There are other issues that can sway these voters.
sentences.zh: 还有其他问题可以左右这些选民。

sentences.en: The border, Biden's age, the war in Israel or something else.
sentences.zh: 边境问题、拜登的年龄、以色列战争或其他事情。

sentences.en: It's not so simple as to say that their vote will be dictated exclusively by the economy.
sentences.zh: 不能简单地说他们的投票将完全由经济决定。

sentences.en: But I think it's fair to say that with all of the huge issues that loom over the country today and how polarized our country is,
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，考虑到今天笼罩在这个国家的所有巨大问题以及我们国家极化的程度，

sentences.en: that an improving economy may not be the same kind of wind in Joe Biden's sails that it was for Harry Truman in 1948.
sentences.zh: 经济好转可能不会像1948年对哈里·杜鲁门那样，成为乔·拜登的助推力。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, thank you very much for the history lesson and the analysis.
sentences.zh: 好的，内特，非常感谢你的历史课和分析。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the United States and its allies carried out a barrage of attacks on Iranian forces and the militias they support.
sentences.zh: 周末，美国及其盟友对伊朗军队及其支持的民兵发动了一连串袭击。

sentences.en: The strikes began on Friday, targeting sites in Syria and Iraq in response to attacks that killed three American soldiers in Jordan and injured at least 40 more U.S.
sentences.zh: 袭击始于周五，目标是叙利亚和伊拉克的地点，以回应导致三名美国士兵在约旦死亡、至少40名美国士兵受伤的袭击事件。

sentences.en: troops.
sentences.zh: 部队。

sentences.en: The attacks continued on Saturday and Sunday with U.S.
sentences.zh: 袭击在周六和周日继续进行，美国对也门境内的数十个目标进行了打击，这些目标由伊朗支持的胡塞民兵控制，该民兵一直在威胁红海的全球航运。

sentences.en: strikes against dozens of targets in Yemen, controlled by the Iranian-backed Houthi militia, which has continued to threaten global shipping in the Red Sea.
sentences.zh: 虽然美国表示不寻求扩大中东战争，

sentences.en: While the United States says that it is not looking to widen the war in the Middle East,
sentences.zh: 但过去三天的袭击代表了明显的升级，美国官员表示这远未结束。

sentences.en: the strikes over the past three days represent a clear escalation that American officials said was far from over.
sentences.zh: 我今天没有什么关于这些袭击中具体消灭了谁的消息可以分享，

sentences.en: I don't have anything to share with you today on precisely who was taken out in those strikes,
sentences.zh: 但我只想说，总统在下令并执行这些袭击时很明确，这是我们回应的开始，未来还会有更多步骤。

sentences.en: but I would just say that the president was clear when he ordered them and when he conducted them that that was the beginning of our response and there will be more steps to come.
sentences.zh: 在第一场民主党总统初选中，拜登总统在南卡罗来纳州彻底击败了他的竞争对手，赢得了超过96%的选票。

sentences.en: And in the first Democratic presidential primary, President Biden thoroughly dominated his rivals in South Carolina, winning more than 96 percent of the vote.
sentences.zh: 拜登的竞选团队特别关注黑人选民的投票率，民调显示他们对他的热情不如过去。

sentences.en: Biden's campaign team was especially interested in the turnout of Black voters, who polls show are less enthusiastic about him than in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 拜登的助手表示，周六初选的早期数据显示，南卡罗来纳州黑人选民的比例比2020年高出13%。

sentences.en: Biden's aides said that early data from Saturday's primary showed that the share of Black voters in South Carolina was 13 percent higher than in 2020.

sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。
